results.question: Do I need a visa to visit Japan as a US citizen?
results.reference_answer: Based on the chunks provided, US citizens can enter Japan visa-free for stays of up to 90 days, which is generally valid for tourism purposes. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs maintains an online Guide to Japanese Visas for further information.

runs.final_answer:
As a US citizen, you do not need a visa to visit Japan for a stay of up to 90 days [3].

_Note: this answer rests on a single supporting source (thin grounding) — treat it with extra caution._

Transit without a visa (TWOV)

No visa is required for a same-day transit between international flights at the same airport, so long as you do not leave the secured area.

Visitors with tickets for onward travel to a third country may be granted a
Shore Pass
for a maximum of 72 hours with their permitted stay area limited to the vicinity of the port of entry. The port of departure does not have to be the same as the port of entry. Instead, it only needs to be in its vicinity.

Shore Passes are granted at immigration discretion and airlines may hesitate to allow you to board if you have a multi-day layover and are relying on getting on. Getting a transit visa in advance is always a safer option.

Residence Card

Travellers entering Japan with anything other than a temporary visitor visa are required to obtain a "Residence Card" (在留カード), colloquially known as a
gaijin card
, within 90 days of arrival and carry it at all times in lieu of their passport. Those staying for 90 days or less may complete this registration, but they are not obligated to. This will be invalidated upon exit from Japan, unless a re-entry permit is held.

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Japan?
results.reference_answer: According to the CDC, you should make sure you are up-to-date on all routine vaccines before traveling to Japan. Hepatitis A vaccine is recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old, and Japanese Encephalitis vaccine is recommended for travelers moving to an area with Japanese encephalitis, spending long periods of time there, or frequently traveling to such areas. You should visit your doctor at least a month before your trip to get vaccines or medicines you may need.

runs.final_answer: For travel to Japan, the CDC recommends that all international travelers be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine due to rising global measles cases [1]. Additionally, vaccination for Japanese encephalitis is recommended for travelers who will be living in or spending long periods in areas with Japanese encephalitis, or for those who will be engaging in activities that increase the risk of infection, such as visiting rural areas or camping [4].

Stay Healthy and Safe

Learn actions you can take to stay healthy and safe on your trip. Vaccines cannot protect you from many diseases in Japan, so your behaviors are important.

Eat and drink safely

Food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination. Standards may also differ within a country and risk may change depending on activity type (e.g., hiking versus business trip). You can learn more about safe food and drink choices when traveling by accessing the resources below.

Choose Safe Food and Drinks When Traveling

Water Treatment Options When Hiking, Camping or Traveling

Global Water, Sanitation and Hygiene | Global Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) | CDC

You can also visit the
Department of State Country Information Pages
for additional information about food and water safety.

Prevent bug bites

Although Japan is an industrialized country, bug bites here can still spread diseases. Just as you would in the United States, try to avoid bug bites while spending time outside or in wooded areas.

What can I do to prevent bug bites?

Cover exposed skin by wearing long-sleeved shirts, long pants, and hats.

Use an appropriate insect repellent (see below).

Consider using permethrin-treated clothing and gear if spending a lot of time outside. Do
use permethrin directly on skin.

results.question: What should I visit in Japan?
results.reference_answer: Based on the chunks, you should visit Japan's famous gardens including the official "Top Three Gardens" (Kairakuen in Mito, Kenrokuen, and Korakuen) and Ritsurin Park in Takamatsu, as well as Zen rock/sand gardens at temples like Ryoanji Temple. Other notable destinations include Nijo Castle, Mount Fuji (Japan's iconic snow-topped volcano and highest peak at 3776m), Miyajima with its floating gate, World War II sites in Hiroshima, Nagasaki, and Okinawa, and cities like Kyoto (first capital of a united Japan with many Buddhist shrines and historical buildings) and Nara (ancient Buddhist temples and gardens).

runs.final_answer:
When visiting Japan, you have a variety of attractions to consider. You can explore the country's feudal heritage by visiting sites of nobility and samurai clans that date back to the pre-industrial era [1]. For winter sports enthusiasts, Japan offers excellent skiing and snowboarding opportunities, particularly in the Japanese Alps, known for their deep powder snow [1]. 

If you're interested in Japanese gardens, you can visit some of the nation's famous landscape and Zen rock/sand gardens, which are celebrated for their unique aesthetics [2]. Additionally, participating in a Japanese tea ceremony can provide insight into the country's cultural practices and aesthetics, emphasizing the concept of wabi-sabi, or the beauty of simplicity and age [3].

For a mix of cultural influences, you might visit Nagasaki, an ancient port city with a blend of Chinese, Japanese, and European influences [4]. If you're interested in historical architecture, the Kansai region, including cities like Kyoto and Osaka, offers many Buddhist shrines and historical buildings [4]. 

Lastly, for a unique experience, consider exploring Japan's lesser-known destinations, which offer fascinating sights off the beaten track [4].

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Mexico?
results.reference_answer: According to the CDC, recommended vaccinations for Mexico include Hepatitis A for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older, and travelers should be up to date with routine vaccines including COVID-19, Measles-Mumps-Rubella (MMR), and others. Chikungunya vaccination may be considered for extended stays of 6 months or more, and anti-malarial medications are recommended for certain regions including Campeche, Chiapas, and southern Chihuahua state.

runs.final_answer:
For travel to Mexico, the CDC recommends the following vaccinations and health precautions:

1. **Routine Vaccinations**: Ensure you are up to date with routine vaccinations such as Varicella, Diphtheria-Tetanus-Pertussis (DTaP, Tdap, or Td), Flu (influenza), Measles-Mumps-Rubella (MMR), Polio, and Shingles [6].

2. **COVID-19**: All eligible travelers should be up to date with their COVID-19 vaccines [6].

3. **Hepatitis A**: Recommended for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older. Infants 6 to 11 months old should also be vaccinated against Hepatitis A [6].

4. **Chikungunya**: There is an elevated risk of chikungunya in Mexico. Vaccination may be considered for those planning to stay for an extended period (e.g., 6 months or more) [6].

5. **Malaria**: For areas like Campeche, Chiapas, and the southern part of Chihuahua state, chemoprophylaxis is recommended. In other areas with malaria transmission, insect bite precautions and mosquito avoidance are advised [2].

Additionally, travelers should take precautions against New World screwworm myiasis by cleaning and covering wounds, sleeping in screened areas, and avoiding livestock [1].

results.question: How safe is it to travel in Mexico right now?
results.reference_answer: The U.S. Department of State has issued a Level 2 Travel Advisory for Mexico, advising Americans to "Exercise increased caution" due to terrorism and crime, with many violent crimes including homicide, kidnapping, carjacking, sexual assault, and robbery taking place in Mexico. However, one source notes that "the average traveller should not be too overly concerned or cautious of their surroundings" as "a lot of the crime occurs between those involved in the drug trade or organised crime." Specific states have varying risk levels, with some areas at Level 3 (Reconsider travel) or Level 4 (Do not travel).

runs.final_answer:
Traveling in Mexico requires exercising increased caution due to various safety concerns. The U.S. Department of State has issued a Level 2 travel advisory for Mexico, advising travelers to exercise increased caution due to crime and kidnapping in some areas [2]. Additionally, demonstrations can occur frequently, sometimes blocking roads or bridges, and travelers should be prepared for such disruptions [1]. 

Health risks are also a consideration, with issues like carbon monoxide poisoning reported due to a lack of detectors in some accommodations [1]. Moreover, travelers should be aware of health concerns such as malaria in certain regions and take appropriate precautions [6]. 

While Mexico has a reputation for being dangerous, much of the crime is related to drug trafficking and organized crime, and the average traveler should not be overly concerned if they remain cautious and aware of their surroundings [7].

results.question: What should I visit in Mexico?
results.reference_answer: Based on the retrieved chunks, you should visit Mexico City, the capital with a 700-year history featuring parks, Aztec ruins, colonial architecture, and museums. You can also explore archaeological sites like Chichen Itza, Teotihuacan, Tulum, and Palenque, as well as natural attractions including Copper Canyon, the Sea of Cortez for whale watching and swimming with dolphins, Monarch Butterfly Reserves in Michoacán, and Sumidero Canyon. Mexico has 35 UNESCO world heritage sites as of 2018, more than anywhere else in the Americas, and over 100 scenic small towns designated as Pueblos Mágicos.

runs.final_answer:
When visiting Mexico, you might consider exploring some of its vibrant destinations and cultural sites. Mazatlán is a lively Pacific coast town known for its beaches and as a popular Spring Break destination [3]. Monterrey, a large modern city in Northern Mexico, offers a dry, mountainous setting and is recognized for its educational and transportation infrastructure [3]. Puebla, located southeast of Mexico City, is one of the country's largest and oldest cities and is famous for its Cinco de Mayo celebrations [3].

Additionally, Mexico boasts 35 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, which include cultural sites related to pre-Columbian civilizations and early colonial cities [6]. The country also offers opportunities to explore its diverse wildlife and natural landscapes, including mountains and volcanoes [6].

results.question: What should I visit in Singapore?
results.reference_answer: In Singapore, you should visit beaches and tourist resorts on Sentosa or its southern islands, cultural areas like Chinatown for Chinese treats and Little India for Indian flavours, and the colonial core in the Bras Basah area with historical buildings and museums. For nature and wildlife, popular attractions include Singapore Zoo, Night Safari, Jurong Bird Park, Botanic Gardens, and the futuristic Gardens by the Bay in the Marina district. Religious sites worth visiting include Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery, Sri Mariamman Temple, the Burmese Buddhist Temple, and Masjid Sultan in Arab Street.

runs.final_answer:
In Singapore, you should consider visiting several notable attractions:

1. **Cultural and Religious Sites**: Explore the diverse religious sites such as the Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery, the colorful Sri Mariamman Temple, the Burmese Buddhist Temple, and the stately Masjid Sultan on Arab Street [5].

2. **Historical and Museum Districts**: The Bras Basah area is Singapore's colonial core, featuring historical buildings and museums [2].

3. **Marina Bay**: This area is dominated by the Marina Bay Sands integrated resort, the futuristic Gardens by the Bay, and the Marina Barrage. It also includes the Singapore Flyer and the Esplanade Theatres, contributing to the iconic skyline of Singapore [8].

4. **Riverside (Civic District)**: Known for its museums, statues, theatres, and vibrant nightlife along the banks of the Singapore River at Boat Quay and Clarke Quay [8].

These sites offer a mix of cultural, historical, and modern attractions that highlight the diversity and vibrancy of Singapore.

About Singapore

Singapore is located in Southeast Asia, in both the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres. It has maritime borders with Malaysia, Indonesia, the Straits of Malacca and the South China Sea. It shares no direct land borders with any country but is connected to Malaysia by two causeways.

Cases of measles are on the rise worldwide. Travelers are at risk of measles if they have not been fully vaccinated at least two weeks prior to departure, or have not had measles in the past, and travel internationally to areas where measles is spreading.

All international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine, including an early dose for infants 6–11 months, according to
CDC’s measles vaccination recommendations for international travel

Measles (Rubeola) - CDC Yellow Book

Rabies

Dogs infected with rabies are not commonly found in South Korea.

Rabies is present in some terrestrial wildlife species.

If rabies exposures occur while in South Korea, rabies vaccines are typically available throughout most of the country.

Rabies pre-exposure vaccination considerations include whether travelers 1) will be performing occupational or recreational activities that increase risk for exposure to potentially rabid animals and 2) might have difficulty getting prompt access to safe post-exposure prophylaxis.

Please consult with a healthcare provider to determine whether you should receive pre-exposure vaccination before travel.

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for South Korea?
results.reference_answer: According to the CDC, you should make sure you are up-to-date on all routine vaccines before traveling to South Korea. Recommended vaccines include hepatitis A for all travelers, hepatitis B for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60, and Japanese encephalitis for certain travelers depending on their activities and length of stay. The MMR vaccine is recommended as measles cases are rising worldwide, and travelers should be fully vaccinated at least two weeks prior to departure.

runs.final_answer: For travel to South Korea, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that travelers be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine due to rising global measles cases [1]. Additionally, the CDC advises that unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old should consider getting vaccinated for Hepatitis B before traveling to South Korea [7].

Sexual assault and domestic violence

The Embassy receives reports of sexual assault from U.S. citizens.

Most cases involve young women assaulted by people they met on social media or dating and messaging apps.

Alcohol is often involved, and South Korea’s low overall crime rate can create a false sense of security.

Specialized hospital units and police are available in South Korea to assist victims.

Services in English and responsiveness to these crimes are inconsistent.

U.S. citizen victims of domestic violence are encouraged to contact the nearest U.S. embassy and local law enforcement for assistance.

There are victim’s assistance resources, including women’s shelters, in Seoul and other urban areas, but resources may be limited in rural areas.

There are no specific advisories against travel to South Korea, suggesting that it is relatively safe to visit at this time.

results.question: What should I visit in South Korea?
results.reference_answer: In South Korea, you should visit Seoul, the 600-year-old capital where you'll find palaces like Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung, the National Museum of Korea, and the Fortress Wall with the famous Namdaemun gate. You can also visit the DMZ 'truce village' and the Third Tunnel of Aggression about 44 km from Seoul, Bukhansan National Park with the Bukhansanseong Fortress, Busan (the second city and main beach destination), Gyeongju (the ancient capital of the Silla Kingdom), and Jeju (South Korea's honeymoon island created by a volcano with great scenery).

runs.final_answer:
In South Korea, you should consider visiting several key destinations. Seoul, the dynamic 600-year-old capital, offers a fusion of ancient and modern attractions [3]. Busan, the second-largest city, is known for its beaches [3]. Jeju Island, often referred to as South Korea's honeymoon island, features volcanic landscapes, wildflowers, and opportunities for horseback riding [3]. Additionally, Chuncheon, surrounded by lakes and mountains, is famous for local dishes like dakgalbi and makguksu [3].

Be wary in these areas if you have any respiratory problems (including asthma).

results.question: What should I visit in New Zealand?
results.reference_answer: New Zealand offers stunning and diverse natural beauty including the Southern Alps, national parks, mountains, lakes and glaciers. Notable destinations include Aoraki / Mount Cook National Park with New Zealand's highest mountain, Milford Sound (one of New Zealand's most spectacular fiords), Tongariro National Park with three volcanoes, and geothermal areas around Rotorua with geysers and hot springs. It's also worthwhile to spend some time in the cities, such as Wellington (the national capital with the Te Papa museum), Auckland (the City of Sails), and Christchurch (the Garden City).

runs.final_answer: You should visit several places in New Zealand known for their natural beauty and cultural significance. The country is renowned for its stunning and diverse landscapes, including jagged mountains, rolling pasture land, steep fiords, pristine lakes, raging rivers, scenic beaches, and active volcanic zones [4]. Additionally, you can explore cities like Wellington, the national capital, which features the Parliament and Beehive buildings and the Te Papa museum [6].

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Egypt?
results.reference_answer: According to the CDC, recommended vaccinations for Egypt include routine vaccines (measles-mumps-rubella, diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis, varicella, polio, and yearly flu), Hepatitis A and typhoid fever, Hepatitis B for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 (with those 60 and older potentially getting vaccinated), and Rabies if planning outdoor activities or a long stay. Health precautions include eating and drinking safely, preventing bug bites, avoiding contaminated water, and staying hydrated in Egypt's extremely dry climate.

runs.final_answer: For travel to Egypt, it is recommended that travelers be up to date on all routine vaccinations, including the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine, due to rising measles cases globally [1][3]. Additionally, the CDC recommends the Hepatitis A vaccine for travelers to Egypt, as the disease can be contracted through contaminated food or water [3]. The Hepatitis B vaccine is also recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old, and those 60 and older may consider vaccination before traveling [3]. It is important to practice safe food and water precautions to avoid non-vaccine-preventable diseases [6].

results.question: How safe is it to travel in Egypt right now?
results.reference_answer: Egypt has a Level 2 travel advisory ("Exercise increased caution") due to terrorism, crime, and health concerns, with some areas like the Northern and Middle Sinai Peninsula under "Do not travel" warnings due to terrorism. While Egypt is often labeled as unsafe by foreign governments, "the average traveller should not be too overly concerned or cautious of their surroundings," and traveling in Egypt is "more or less, similar to travelling in Morocco, Jordan, Palestine, Turkey."

runs.final_answer: Traveling in Egypt is generally considered safe, though it is often labeled as unsafe by many foreign governments. However, the average traveler should not be overly concerned or overly cautious about their surroundings [2]. It is important to stay informed about travel advisories and follow guidance from official sources such as the U.S. Department of State [3]. Additionally, travelers should practice usual health precautions as advised by the CDC [4].

results.question: What should I visit in Egypt?
results.reference_answer: In Egypt, you can visit the world-famous pyramids, temples, and see mummies, art, churches, mosques, and hieroglyphics. Popular destinations include Cairo with Islamic Cairo/Khan El Khalili and the pyramids at Saqqara, Alexandria with the Bibliotheca Alexandrina and Qa'edbay's Castle, Luxor and Aswan for impressive temples and ancient monuments including a Nile cruise, and Abu Simbel near Lake Nasser, which is one of the most impressive sights in Egypt besides the pyramids.

runs.final_answer:
When visiting Egypt, travelers should consider exploring the following attractions:

1. The Pyramids and temples of Saqqara, located just north of Dahshur, are a must-see for those interested in ancient Egyptian history [5].
2. Memphis, which houses relics of ancient Egypt, including a huge statue of Ramesses II [5].
3. The Bibliotheca Alexandrina in Alexandria, along with Qa'edbay's Castle and other Roman and Greek sights [5].
4. Aswan, situated next to the Nile, offers impressive temples and ancient monuments, as well as the Tombs of Nobles [5].
5. A felucca cruise on the Nile is a popular way to experience Upper Egypt [2].

These sites offer a glimpse into Egypt's rich history and cultural heritage.

results.question: How safe is it to travel in Greece right now?
results.reference_answer: Greece has a Level 1 travel advisory ("Exercise normal precautions") and is described as "a generally safe destination for travelers." Petty crime such as pick-pocketing and purse-snatching is common, especially at popular tourist sites and on public transportation like the metro, and the greatest danger to travelers is likely traffic, as Greece has one of the highest traffic fatality rates in the European Union.

runs.final_answer:
The safety of traveling in Greece right now can be assessed from several perspectives:

1. **Health and Safety Precautions**: The CDC advises practicing usual precautions when traveling to Greece, indicating a relatively low level of health risk. However, travelers should be aware of the global rise in measles cases and ensure they are vaccinated against measles before traveling [3].

2. **Environmental Concerns**: Greece experiences extreme heat during the summer, which can lead to health issues such as heat exhaustion and heatstroke. Travelers are advised to stay hydrated, avoid peak sun hours, and seek shade or air conditioning to mitigate these risks [7].

Overall, while there are some health and environmental considerations to keep in mind, Greece is generally safe for travel with the appropriate precautions.

results.question: What should I visit in Greece?
results.reference_answer: Greece offers numerous attractions including the Parthenon in Athens, the archaeological sites of Delphi, Olympia, Mycenae and Tiryns, the hilltop monasteries of Meteora, and islands like Santorini (known for beautiful views and sunsets), Mykonos, Rhodes, and Crete. Visitors can also explore the Sanctuary of Asklepios at Epidaurus, the Temple of Hera and Tunnel of Eupalinos on Samos, and enjoy Greece's 16,000 kms of coastline with numerous beaches and seaside resorts.

runs.final_answer:
In Greece, there are several must-visit destinations that offer a mix of historical, cultural, and natural attractions. Delphi is renowned for its archaeological site and the famous oracle of Apollo[4]. Meteora is notable for its hilltop monasteries, providing stunning views and a unique spiritual experience[4]. The island of Mykonos is famous for its sophisticated holiday atmosphere[4]. Olympia is an ancient sanctuary dedicated to Zeus and the site of the ancient Olympics[4]. Rhodes offers ancient monuments and beautiful beaches[4]. Santorini, known for its volcanic landscapes, offers breathtaking views, charming towns, and spectacular sunsets[4]. These destinations highlight the diverse offerings of Greece, from historical sites to beautiful islands.

_Note: this answer rests on a single supporting source (thin grounding) — treat it with extra caution._

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Israel?
results.reference_answer: Based on CDC recommendations for Israel, the West Bank and Gaza, travelers should consider vaccinations for Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B (recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60), measles (MMR vaccine), and be up to date on polio vaccines. If your trip includes the West Bank and Gaza, you might want to consider getting typhoid vaccine and rabies pre-exposure vaccination depending on your activities and risk of exposure to potentially rabid animals.

runs.final_answer:
For travel to Israel, the CDC recommends several vaccinations and health precautions:

1. **Hepatitis A**: Infants aged 6 to 11 months should be vaccinated against Hepatitis A. Unvaccinated travelers over 40 years old, those who are immunocompromised, or have chronic medical conditions should receive the initial dose of the vaccine and immune globulin if traveling to a risk area in less than two weeks [1].

2. **Hepatitis B**: Recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old [1].

3. **Polio**: Ensure you are up to date on your polio vaccines due to circulating poliovirus in some international destinations [2].

4. **Rabies**: Rabies is present in Israel, the West Bank, and Gaza. Pre-exposure vaccination should be considered for travelers who might be exposed to potentially rabid animals or have difficulty accessing post-exposure prophylaxis [6].

5. **Measles**: Be aware of rising measles cases globally and ensure vaccinations are up to date [2].

These recommendations are based on the CDC's guidelines for travelers to Israel, the West Bank, and Gaza [1][2][6].

Prevent bug bites

Although Israel, the West Bank and Gaza is an industrialized country, bug bites here can still spread diseases. Just as you would in the United States, try to avoid bug bites while spending time outside or in wooded areas.

What can I do to prevent bug bites?

Cover exposed skin by wearing long-sleeved shirts, long pants, and hats.

Use an appropriate insect repellent (see below).

Consider using permethrin-treated clothing and gear if spending a lot of time outside. Do
use permethrin directly on skin.

Reduce your exposure to germs

Follow these tips to avoid getting sick or spreading illness to others while traveling:

Wash your hands often, especially before eating.

If soap and water aren’t available, clean hands with hand sanitizer (containing at least 60% alcohol).

Don’t touch your eyes, nose, or mouth. If you need to touch your face, make sure your hands are clean.

Cover your mouth and nose with a tissue or your sleeve (not your hands) when coughing or sneezing.

Try to avoid contact with people who are sick.

If you are sick, stay home or in your hotel room, unless you need medical care.

Avoid sharing body fluids

Diseases can be spread through body fluids, such as saliva, blood, vomit, and semen.

Protect yourself:

Use latex condoms correctly.

Do not inject drugs.

Limit alcohol consumption. People take more risks when intoxicated.

Do not share needles or any devices that can break the skin. That includes needles for tattoos, piercings, and acupuncture.

If you receive medical or dental care, make sure the equipment is disinfected or sanitized.

results.question: What should I visit in Israel?
results.reference_answer: Israel contains a wide variety of sites to visit, including religious sites like the Western Wall, natural sites like the Dead Sea (the lowest place on earth) and the Mediterranean coastline with beaches, and historic sites like Masada (a mountaintop fortress) and Roman cities such as Caesarea. There are about 75 national parks and nature reserves, and cities like Jerusalem (with its historic Old City sacred to three religions) and Tel Aviv (known for its Bauhaus architecture, beaches, and markets). The country also offers hiking trails, the Ramon crater (the world's largest erosion crater), and is one of the world's best places for bird watching.

runs.final_answer:
When visiting Israel, there are several notable sites and attractions to consider:

1. **Natural Sites**: The Dead Sea is a unique natural wonder, being the lowest place on earth with extremely salty water that allows you to float effortlessly [1]. Israel also offers beautiful Mediterranean beaches and opportunities for scuba diving in the Red Sea [1].

2. **Historic Sites**: The City of David in Jerusalem offers a glimpse into ancient history with remains from the time of King David [4]. The Old City of Jerusalem is another must-visit, with its rich religious and historical significance, including sites like the Dome of the Rock, the Western Wall, and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [5].

3. **Cultural Experiences**: Markets such as Machaneh Yehudah in Jerusalem and Carmel Market in Tel Aviv provide vibrant cultural experiences that reflect the local lifestyle [1].

4. **Art and Spirituality**: Safed (Tzfat) is known for its artistic community and spiritual significance, being a center for Kabbalah [5].

5. **National Parks and Trails**: Israel has about 75 national parks and nature reserves, offering well-maintained trails and historical insights [2]. Hiking opportunities abound, with trails like those in the Ramon Crater or the Negev desert [3].

These sites offer a mix of natural beauty, historical depth, and cultural richness, making them worthwhile destinations for travelers in Israel.

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Peru?
results.reference_answer: The vaccines most commonly needed to travel to Peru are against tetanus, diphtheria, typhoid fever, hepatitis A and B, yellow fever, rabies and meningitis. Yellow fever vaccination is recommended for travelers going to areas below 2,300 m elevation in certain regions including Amazonas, Cusco, Huánuco, Junín, Loreto, Madre de Dios, Pasco, Puno, San Martín, and Ucayali. Malaria prophylaxis with atovaquone-proguanil, doxycycline, mefloquine, or tafenoquine is recommended for areas below 2,500 m elevation east of the Andes.

runs.final_answer: For travel to Peru, it is recommended that travelers be up to date with their COVID-19 vaccines [2]. Additionally, vaccination against Hepatitis A is recommended for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older, and infants 6 to 11 months old should also be vaccinated against Hepatitis A [2]. There is also an elevated risk of chikungunya in Peru, and vaccination may be considered for those staying for an extended period [2]. Malaria prophylaxis is recommended for areas below 2,500 meters elevation east of the Andes [4]. Measles vaccination is advised due to rising cases worldwide [4].

Food safety

Enjoy the food, but be judicious, lest you contract
diarrhea
, dysentery, or a more serious disease such as a parasitic infestation that could ruin your trip. Thoroughly cooked food is most likely to be safe. Food that's been left out too long or landed on by flies could make you sick. Seafood can go bad particularly easily. results.question: How safe is it to travel in Peru right now?
results.reference_answer: Peru has a Level 2 Travel Advisory ("Exercise Increased Caution") due to crime, civil unrest, and the risk of kidnapping. Crime is common in Peru, with petty theft, carjackings, muggings, assaults, and other violent crime often happening even in daylight hours and with many witnesses. Certain specific areas have Level 4 advisories ("Do Not Travel"), including the Colombia-Peru border area in the Loreto Region and the VRAEM region.

runs.final_answer: Traveling in Peru currently requires increased caution due to several factors. Demonstrations can occur without warning, leading to road closures that disrupt travel between cities and access to public transportation and airports [1]. Additionally, heavy rainfall has caused major flooding in multiple districts, increasing the risk of waterborne diseases and making land travel dangerous in affected areas [2]. The U.S. State Department advises exercising increased caution due to crime, civil unrest, and the risk of kidnapping, with certain areas having a higher risk [7].

results.question: What should I visit in Peru?
results.reference_answer: Peru offers forgotten temples in dense Amazon jungles, lost Inca cities, fabulous wildlife and extraordinary folklore. Key sites include Machu Picchu (a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the most famous sets of ruins in the world), the Nazca Lines (world-famous for its geometrical figures and giant drawings in the desert sand), Cusco (once the capital of the Inca Empire), Colca Canyon (Peru's third most-visited destination), and Manú National Park (one of the most diverse areas in Peru with over 15,000 plant species).

runs.final_answer: When visiting Peru, travelers should consider exploring the Inca Highlands, which are known for their stunning Inca sites and the beautiful city of Cusco, once the capital of the Inca Empire [3]. Additionally, the Peruvian Amazon offers a vast jungle region in the Amazon basin, providing opportunities to experience extraordinary wildlife and folklore [5]. For those interested in cultural experiences, Lima, the capital city, offers a mix of modern and colonial architecture and is a great place to enjoy Peruvian cuisine [5].

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Morocco?
results.reference_answer: According to the CDC, recommended vaccinations for Morocco include Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B (recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old), and measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine. The CDC also notes that "no particular inoculations are needed for Morocco under normal circumstances," though it makes good sense to have a recent tetanus immunization and to consider Hepatitis A and B inoculations.

runs.final_answer: For travel to Morocco, it is recommended to be vaccinated against Hepatitis A and B. Hepatitis A vaccination is advised for all travelers, while Hepatitis B vaccination is recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old. Those over 60 may also consider getting vaccinated before traveling [1][2]. Additionally, while no specific inoculations are required under normal circumstances, it is sensible to have a recent tetanus immunization [3]. Rabies is a concern in Morocco, so travelers potentially exposed should seek medical care immediately [2].

General concerns

Inoculations
: No particular inoculations are needed for Morocco under normal circumstances, but check with the
US's Centre for Disease Control (CDC) travel web pages
for any recent disease outbreaks. As with most travel, it makes good sense to have a recent tetanus immunization. Consider Hepatitis A and B inoculations.

Food and drink
: Avoid uncooked fruits and vegetables that you can not peel. Avoid any food that is not prepared when you order it (e.g. buffets). Usually fried and boiled foods are safe. Some travellers have also had problems with unrefrigerated condiments (such as mayonnaise) used in fast food outlets.

Water
: It is advisable to drink bottled water (check that the cap is sealed - some people might try to sell you tap water in recycled bottles). Be wary of ice or cordials that may be made with tap water. Some hotels provide free bottled water to guests and it's wise to keep a supply in your room so as not to be tempted with tap water.

Shoes
: Keep your sandals for the beach. Moroccan streets double as garbage disposal areas and you may not want to wade through fish heads and chicken parts with open-toe shoes.

Malaria
: Present in the northern, coastal areas of the country but not a major problem. Take the usual precautions

results.question: What should I visit in Morocco?
results.reference_answer: Based on the chunks, you should visit Morocco's imperial cities including Marrakech to see the Saadian Tombs, El Badi Palace, Koutoubia Mosque, and Jamaa el-Fnaa square; Fes (once Morocco's capital) for its medina, University of Al-Karaouine, Bou Inania Madrasa, and leather tanning factories; and coastal towns like Asilah for a laid-back medina experience. Other destinations include the High Atlas mountains for hiking, the Sahara desert dunes at Erg Chebbi near Merzouga or Erg Chigaga near M'Hamid for camel rides, and cities like Rabat (the capital), Casablanca for its contemporary mosque, and Tangier as a ferry entry point from Spain.

runs.final_answer:
To experience the best of Morocco, you should consider visiting its bustling souqs and spice markets, which offer a sensory overload of colors, smells, and sounds. The country is also home to stunning mosques and white-washed seaside towns, as well as medieval city centers that provide a glimpse into its rich history. For breathtaking natural landscapes, the snow-covered peaks of the High Atlas and the endless sand dunes of the Sahara are must-see destinations [4].

_Note: this answer rests on a single supporting source (thin grounding) — treat it with extra caution._

Food and drink
: Avoid uncooked fruits and vegetables that you can not peel. Avoid any food that is not prepared when you order it (e.g. buffets). Usually fried and boiled foods are safe. Some travellers have also had problems with unrefrigerated condiments (such as mayonnaise) used in fast food outlets.

Water

About Italy

Italy is a peninsula in southern Europe, shaped like a boot. It has a maritime border on the Mediterranean Sea to the west, south, and east. It has land borders with France, Switzerland, Austria, and Slovenia. Italy also includes the islands of Sicily and Sardinia.

Italy is slightly larger than the state of Arizona. It has 1 time zone called Central European Time (CET), which is 6 hours ahead of Washington, D.C.

San Marino is a fully autonomous, independent republic. It is surrounded by north-central Italy. It isn’t part of the EU but has an open border agreement with Italy, so there’s no passport control at its border. San Marino is about 1/3 the size of Washington DC. It uses the euro currency.

About Vatican City

Vatican City is a city-state fully within Rome, Italy. It isn’t part of the EU but has an open border agreement with Italy, so there’s no passport control at its border with Rome. results.question: How safe is it to travel in Italy right now?
results.reference_answer: The U.S. State Department has issued a Level 2 travel advisory for Italy, advising travelers to "Exercise increased caution" due to terrorism. There is risk of terrorist violence, including terrorist attacks and other activity in Italy, with terrorist groups and individuals wanting to attack U.S. citizens and often targeting crowds at high-profile public events, hotels, restaurants, places of worship, and public transportation systems.

runs.final_answer: The safety of traveling in Italy right now involves several considerations. The U.S. Department of State advises travelers to exercise increased caution due to the potential for terrorism, as terrorist groups may target public events and places frequented by tourists [2]. Additionally, travelers should be aware of potential strikes and work stoppages that could affect transportation, such as airlines and trains [3]. There is also a risk of theft in crowded tourist areas and on public transportation [5]. Natural hazards such as flooding in Venice, avalanches in mountainous areas, and volcanic activity, particularly near Mt. Etna in Sicily, should also be considered [6]. Despite these risks, the CDC advises practicing usual precautions, indicating a relatively low health risk level [7].

About Italy

Italy is a peninsula in southern Europe, shaped like a boot. It has a maritime border on the Mediterranean Sea to the west, south, and east. It has land borders with France, Switzerland, Austria, and Slovenia. Italy also includes the islands of Sicily and Sardinia.

Italy is slightly larger than the state of Arizona. It has 1 time zone called Central European Time (CET), which is 6 hours ahead of Washington, D.C.

About San Marino

San Marino is a fully autonomous, independent republic. It is surrounded by north-central Italy. It isn’t part of the EU but has an open border agreement with Italy, so there’s no passport control at its border. San Marino is about 1/3 the size of Washington DC. It uses the euro currency.

About Vatican City

Vatican City is a city-state fully within Rome, Italy. It isn’t part of the EU but has an open border agreement with Italy, so there’s no passport control at its border with Rome. The Holy See governs the Roman Catholic Church and is based in Vatican City. It is less than 1/4 of a mile in size, making it the smallest coun

The tradition of cheese in Sardinia is ancient and important and the exports of its pecorino cheese have contributed to ensuring this classic Made in Italy product is renowned worldwide. results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for India?
results.reference_answer: According to CDC guidelines, travelers to India should visit their doctor at least 1 month before travel to update vaccinations. Recommended or required vaccinations include yellow fever (required if arriving from areas with risk of yellow fever), hepatitis A, typhoid (especially for those staying with friends or relatives or visiting smaller cities or rural areas), and rabies (recommended for long stays, children, travelers in rural areas, and those with potential exposure to animals). Additional vaccines to consider include influenza, measles-mumps-rubella, COVID-19, and chikungunya (for extended stays of 6 months or more), and travelers going to certain areas should take prescription medicine to prevent malaria.

runs.final_answer: For travel to India, it is recommended to update your vaccinations according to CDC guidelines, which include vaccinations for hepatitis, typhoid, and rabies, especially if you plan to stay long-term, travel to rural areas, or have potential exposure to animals [1][2][4]. Proof of yellow fever vaccination is required if you are arriving from areas with a risk of yellow fever [1]. Additionally, consider vaccinations for influenza, particularly if traveling during the flu season [1]. There is also an elevated risk of chikungunya and cholera, so precautions such as avoiding unsafe food and water are advised, and vaccinations may be considered depending on your travel plans [7].

results.question: How safe is it to travel in India right now?
results.reference_answer: According to the U.S. State Department, India has a Level 2 travel advisory to "Exercise increased caution" due to crime and terrorism, with violent crime and terrorism occurring in India and rape being one of the fastest growing crimes. Some areas have increased risk, including Manipur (Level 4 - Do not travel due to violence and crime), northeastern states (Level 3 - Reconsider travel due to violence), and parts of Central and East India (Do not travel due to terrorism). Additionally, travel by road in India is dangerous, as India leads the world in traffic-related deaths.

runs.final_answer: The safety of traveling in India right now involves several considerations. The U.S. Department of State advises travelers to exercise increased caution due to crime and terrorism [3]. Travelers should be aware of their surroundings, understand local customs, and monitor local news [7]. Swimming in open waters along the Indian coastline requires caution due to strong currents and the risk of drowning, particularly during the monsoon season [2]. Additionally, travelers should be cautious of counterfeit rabies vaccines and consider vaccination if at risk [4]. It's also important to ensure water safety by using bottled water from major brands and ensuring the seal is intact [6].

Be cautious swimming in open waters along the Indian coastline.

Strong currents cause drowning every year in areas like Goa, Mumbai, Puri (Odisha) and the Bay of Bengal.

Treat all animals, even those marked as “tame,” as wild and dangerous.

Stay in vehicles or protected enclosures while in game parks or on safaris.

Trekking safety

Stick to routes identified by local authorities.

Use only registered trekking agencies, porters, and guides.

Avoid trekking after dark.

Camp only at designated sites.

Travel in groups.

Popular trekking spots can reach altitudes over 25,000 feet (7,620 meters).

Ensure you are fit for high altitudes and have medical insurance that includes evacuation coverage.

Train travel safety

Train travel is generally safe in India.

India has the third largest railway network in the world.

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Turkey?
results.reference_answer: According to the CDC, recommended vaccinations for Turkey include Hepatitis B for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old, Hepatitis A, and measles (MMR vaccine) for all international travelers. The Turkish Ministry of Health advises tourists to be vaccinated against hepatitis A and B, meningitis (meningococcal vaccine), and tetanus. Additionally, travelers should make sure they are up-to-date on all routine vaccines, and proof of yellow fever vaccination is required if arriving from countries in South America or sub-Saharan Africa where yellow fever is present.

runs.final_answer: For travel to Turkey, the CDC recommends that all international travelers be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine due to rising cases of measles worldwide [2]. Additionally, the Hepatitis A vaccine is recommended for travelers to Turkey. The Hepatitis B vaccine is also recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old, and it may be considered for those 60 and older [3]. There is no mention of yellow fever vaccination requirements unless you are arriving from a country where yellow fever is present [4].

results.question: How safe is it to travel in Turkey right now?
results.reference_answer: The U.S. State Department has issued a Level 2 Travel Advisory for Turkey, advising travelers to "Exercise increased caution" due to terrorism, arbitrary detentions, and other risks. There is a Level 4 "Do not travel" warning for areas within 10 km of Turkey's borders with Syria and Iraq due to terrorism risk, and there are heightened risks of anti-Western sentiment and continued threat of attacks by terrorist groups throughout the country.

runs.final_answer: The safety of traveling in Turkey varies depending on the region. The U.S. State Department advises against travel within 10 km of Turkey's borders with Syria and Iraq due to risks of terrorism and limited emergency services in those areas [7]. However, for the rest of Turkey, travelers are advised to exercise increased caution, especially in light of potential anti-Western sentiment and the risk of terrorist attacks [7]. The CDC suggests practicing usual precautions, with no specific health advisories beyond standard vaccinations [5].

If you go up too fast, you might get altitude sickness. This can cause headaches, dizziness, fatigue, and breathlessness, especially above 2,500 m (8,200 ft).

Safety tips:

Go up slowly in high areas. Take one or more rest days below 3,000 meters to get used to the high altitude.

Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol.

Be aware of the symptoms of altitude sickness and take precautions before you travel.

Very serious problems, such as swelling in the brain (HACE) or fluid in the lungs (HAPE), are emergencies and mean you must go down to a lower altitude right away.

results.question: What should I visit in Turkey?
results.reference_answer: Turkey offers diverse experiences including archaeological sites dating back to neolithic times like Göbekli Tepe, mythical cities like Hattusa, and famous ancient cities like Ephesus, Pergamon, and Troy. You can explore UNESCO World Heritage Sites, cultural routes, nature and eco-life destinations, skiing, beaches, caves, and sustainable destinations like Halfeti, Göynük, and İznik. Istanbul attractions include Hagia Sophia History & Experience Museum and Istanbul Archaeological Museums.

runs.final_answer:
You should consider visiting several notable attractions in Turkey. In Istanbul, you can explore the Hagia Sophia History & Experience Museum and the Istanbul Archaeological Museums, which are part of the city's rich cultural heritage [3]. Additionally, the Ephesus Experience Museum is another significant site that offers a glimpse into Turkey's ancient history [3]. For those interested in unique towns and villages, you might explore Halfeti, which is known for its commitment to sustainability and authentic local experiences [3].

_Note: this answer rests on a single supporting source (thin grounding) — treat it with extra caution._

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Vietnam?
results.reference_answer: Based on CDC recommendations, travelers to Vietnam should consider vaccinations for Hepatitis A (recommended for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older), Hepatitis B (recommended for unvaccinated travelers of all ages), and Japanese Encephalitis (recommended for those moving to the area, spending long periods like a month or more, or frequently traveling to areas with Japanese encephalitis). Additionally, all international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with the MMR vaccine, and travelers should take precautions against mosquito-borne diseases like dengue and malaria through insect bite prevention measures, with malaria chemoprophylaxis recommended for certain provinces.

runs.final_answer: For travel to Vietnam, the CDC recommends several vaccinations and health precautions. It is advised that travelers get vaccinated for Hepatitis A, especially if they are unvaccinated and are one year old or older. Infants aged 6 to 11 months should also receive the Hepatitis A vaccine, although this dose does not count toward the routine 2-dose series [2]. Additionally, travelers should take precautions to prevent mosquito bites, as diseases like dengue, Zika, and filariasis are present in Vietnam and cannot be prevented with vaccines [4][7]. Malaria prophylaxis is recommended for certain provinces, but not for the Mekong and Red River Deltas, where only insect bite precautions are advised [3].

Prevent bug bites

Bugs (like mosquitoes, ticks, and fleas) can spread a number of diseases in Vietnam. Many of these diseases cannot be prevented with a vaccine or medicine. You can reduce your risk by taking steps to prevent bug bites.

What can I do to prevent bug bites?

Cover exposed skin by wearing long-sleeved shirts, long pants, and hats.

Use an appropriate insect repellent (see below).

Use permethrin-treated clothing and gear (such as boots, pants, socks, and tents). Do
use permethrin directly on skin.

Stay and sleep in air-conditioned or screened rooms.

Use a bed net if the area where you are sleeping is exposed to the outdoors.

What type of insect repellent should I use?

FOR PROTECTION AGAINST TICKS AND MOSQUITOES:
Use a repellent that contains 20% or more
DEET
for protection that lasts up to several hours.

FOR PROTECTION AGAINST MOSQUITOES ONLY:
Products with one of the following active ingredients can also help prevent mosquito bites. Higher percentages of active ingredient provide longer protection.

DEET

Vietnam is generally a safe destination for travelers.
Petty crime is common, especially in popular tourist locations. Stay aware of your surroundings.

Do not pick up or approach unknown metal objects in the ground.

results.question: What should I visit in Vietnam?
results.reference_answer: Based on the tourism information, you should visit Vietnam's pristine beaches and idyllic islands, ancient treasures and UNESCO wonders, and breathtaking landscapes while savoring legendary cuisine and celebrating vibrant festivals. Specific destinations mentioned include Ha Long Bay, Hoi An (a historic melting pot of cultures with top Instagrammable spots), Da Nang, Phu Quoc, Nha Trang, Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Sapa, Ha Giang, the Mekong Delta, and Son Doong Cave (Vietnam's natural wonder).

runs.final_answer: When visiting Vietnam, there are several must-see attractions and experiences. You can explore the Mekong Delta, which offers opportunities to drift, cycle, and explore the unique landscape and culture of the region [2]. Another highlight is motorbiking from Hoi An to Hue over the scenic Hai Van Pass, which provides stunning views and an adventurous journey [2]. Additionally, the Phong Nha - Ke Bang National Park is a remarkable destination, known for being the home of the world’s largest cave [8]. For a more tranquil experience, you might consider visiting Pu Luong in Thanh Hoa, often referred to as a hidden paradise [8].

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for China?
results.reference_answer: According to the CDC, you should check the vaccines and medicines list and visit your doctor at least a month before your trip to get vaccines or medicines you may need for China. Recommended vaccinations include routine vaccines, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B (for unvaccinated travelers of all ages), Japanese Encephalitis (depending on travel duration and activities), Typhoid (especially for those staying with friends or relatives or visiting smaller cities or rural areas), and potentially Rabies and Tick-borne Encephalitis based on specific risk factors and activities.

runs.final_answer:
For travel to China, the CDC recommends several vaccinations and health precautions:

1. **Measles**: All international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine due to rising global measles cases [2].

2. **Hepatitis A**: Infants 6 to 11 months old should be vaccinated against Hepatitis A. Unvaccinated travelers over 40, immunocompromised individuals, or those with chronic medical conditions should consider the vaccine and possibly immune globulin if traveling to a risk area soon [7].

3. **Hepatitis B**: Recommended for unvaccinated travelers of all ages traveling to China [7].

4. **Japanese Encephalitis**: Recommended for travelers who might be at risk [7].

Additionally, travelers should practice usual health precautions, such as safe food and water consumption, and be aware of non-vaccine-preventable diseases [2][4].

The U.S. Department of State advises travelers to be aware of increased caution worldwide, including in China, and to follow local laws and travel guidance from the U.S. embassy or consulate [3]. Specific regions such as the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region and Tibet Autonomous Region have extra security measures, including security checks and increased police presence [8]. Travelers should avoid participating in demonstrations, as these could lead to criminal charges [8]. Additionally, using certain technologies like satellite phones and drones requires permits, and failure to comply may result in confiscation, fines, or detention [1]. Health precautions are also advised, such as being cautious about unregulated products and ensuring access to licensed medical facilities [2].

Use the

for a list of health-related items to consider packing for your trip. Talk to your doctor about which items are most important for you.

It’s best to be prepared to prevent and treat common illnesses and injuries. Some supplies and medicines may be difficult to find at your destination, may have different names, or may have different ingredients than what you normally use.

After Your Trip

If you are not feeling well after your trip, you may need to see a doctor. If you need help finding a travel medicine specialist, see
Find a Clinic
. Be sure to tell your doctor about your travel, including where you went and what you did on your trip. Also tell your doctor if you were bitten or scratched by an animal while traveling.

If your doctor prescribed antimalarial medicine for your trip, keep taking the rest of your pills after you return home. If you stop taking your medicine too soon, you could still get sick.

Malaria is always a serious disease and may be a deadly illness.
If you become ill with a fever either while traveling in a malaria-risk area or after you return home (for up to 1 year), you should seek

runs.final_answer:
You should visit several notable attractions in China, including:

1. The Forbidden City in Beijing, which is the world's largest and best-preserved wooden-framed historical palace complex [5].
2. Dazu Rock Carvings, known as the last grand monument of Chinese grotto art [5].
3. Yulong Snow Mountain, a sacred summit of snow and ice [5].
4. The Art of Porcelain-Making in Jingdezhen, where a millennium-old kiln meets global creativity [5].
5. Mount Tai, a symbol of ancient Chinese civilization and belief [5].

These sites offer a glimpse into China's rich cultural heritage and natural beauty.

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Switzerland?
results.reference_answer: According to the State Department, no vaccinations are required for Switzerland. However, the CDC recommends that travelers ensure they are up-to-date on routine vaccines before traveling to Switzerland, and that all international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with the MMR vaccine, as measles cases are rising worldwide.

results.question: How safe is it to travel in Switzerland right now?
results.reference_answer: According to the U.S. State Department, Switzerland has a Level 1 travel advisory ("Exercise normal precautions") issued May 20, 2025, and "Switzerland is generally a safe destination for travelers." Travelers are advised to stay alert in congested and popular tourist areas and be aware of pickpockets, particularly on public transportation and at major railway stations.

runs.final_answer: The current safety situation for traveling in Switzerland is generally positive. The U.S. Department of State advises travelers to exercise increased caution worldwide, but there are no specific warnings or advisories indicating heightened danger in Switzerland at this time [2]. Additionally, the tourism industry in Switzerland is well-regulated, with rules and safety inspections regularly enforced, which contributes to the overall safety for tourists [5]. Health-wise, travelers are advised to practice usual precautions, and there is a specific recommendation to be vaccinated against measles due to rising cases globally [3].

results.question: What should I visit in Switzerland?
results.reference_answer: Based on the provided chunks, you should visit Switzerland's top attractions including the Matterhorn (Switzerland's most famous landmark at 4478 meters high), the Rhine Falls near Schaffhausen (the most famous nature destination in Switzerland), Jungfraujoch (described as putting "a jewel in the crown of any visit to Switzerland"), and Château de Chillon on Lake Geneva (the most visited historical monument in Switzerland).

runs.final_answer:
When visiting Switzerland, you should consider exploring the following attractions:

1. **Matterhorn**: This is Switzerland’s most famous landmark, known for its pyramid-shaped silhouette. It is one of the most photographed mountains in the world, and you can enjoy it through hiking, skiing, or from a viewpoint [3].

2. **Rhine Falls**: Located near Schaffhausen, this is the most famous nature destination in Switzerland. You can experience the massive waterfalls from Laufen Castle, viewing platforms, or on a boat trip [3].

3. **Alpstein Area**: Known for its abrupt and impressive change from the hilly landscape of Central Switzerland to craggy alpine scenery. The area includes the Ebenalp and Wildkirchli, which are accessible via a cableway [5].

4. **Montreux Riviera**: This town is nestled in a sheltered bay on Lake Geneva, offering beautiful scenery and a mild climate [5].

5. **Fribourg/Freiburg**: The Old Town is known for its over 200 unique Gothic facades from the 15th century, providing a medieval charm. You can also climb the Cathedral of St. Nicholas for a stunning view of the town [8].

results.question: Do I need a visa to visit Jordan as a US citizen?
results.reference_answer: Yes, US citizens need a visa to visit Jordan. According to the State Department, "A passport with a validity of at least 6 months and a visa are required" and "A visa is required. You can get a visa on arrival at Queen Alia International Airport and most international land border crossings." Visas can be purchased at borders or airports for 40 JOD, or a Jordan Pass tourist visa can be purchased online prior to travel for 70–80 JOD.

runs.final_answer:
Yes, as a US citizen, you need a visa to visit Jordan. Visas can be purchased at borders or airports for 40 JOD, but these are not considered tourist visas. Alternatively, the Jordan Pass, which acts as a tourist visa, can be purchased prior to travel and costs 70–80 JOD. It is valid for 1 month [6].

_Note: this answer rests on a single supporting source (thin grounding) — treat it with extra caution._

results.reference_answer: Based on the chunks, you should visit Petra, Wadi Rum, and the Dead Sea in Jordan. Wadi Rum offers stunning desert landscapes and is perfect for hiking and exploring. The Dead Sea, known for its unique saltiness and buoyancy, is another popular destination. Additionally, the Baptism Site of Jesus Christ provides a blend of faith, history, and peace [4][6].

About Jordan

Jordan is located in the Middle East, in the Northern Hemisphere. It has maritime borders with the Dead Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba. It has land borders with Syria, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, and Israel.

The country is slightly smaller than Indiana. The time zone is Arabia Standard Time. Jordan is 7 hours ahead of Washington, DC, and does not observe daylight saving time.

Travel requirements

You can also apply using the
Visa E Application
through the Ministry of Interior.

Visitors traveling to Jordan on certain visas will need to meet certain registration requirements with Jordanian police.  Please consult the
Embassy of Jordan's
website for details.

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Canada?
results.reference_answer: According to the State Department, vaccinations are not required for Canada. However, the CDC recommends certain vaccines: Hepatitis B is recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old, and all international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with the MMR vaccine.

runs.final_answer:
For travel to Canada, the CDC recommends that travelers ensure they are vaccinated against hepatitis A, especially if they plan to visit areas where they might be exposed through food or water, such as eating street food [3]. Additionally, hepatitis B vaccination is recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old, and it may be considered for those 60 years and older [3]. Measles vaccination is also advised for all international travelers if they have not been fully vaccinated or have not had measles in the past, due to rising cases worldwide [3].

_Note: this answer rests on a single supporting source (thin grounding) — treat it with extra caution._

results.question: How safe is it to travel in Canada right now?
results.reference_answer: Canada has a Level 1 travel advisory ("Exercise normal precautions") and is generally a safe destination for travelers. Petty crime such as pickpockets may target tourists in busy areas, car thefts are increasing in some cities, and demonstrations occur frequently but past demonstrations have rarely been violent in Canada.

runs.final_answer:
The safety of traveling in Canada right now involves several considerations. The U.S. Department of State advises travelers to exercise increased caution when visiting Canada, but does not specify a higher level of alert such as "reconsider travel" or "do not travel" [3]. Additionally, there are some safety concerns such as "smash and grab" thefts and car thefts in certain cities, and travelers are advised to avoid parking on the street or in unmonitored lots, and to be cautious of pickpockets in busy tourist areas [7].

From a health perspective, the CDC indicates that travelers should practice usual precautions and be aware of a hepatitis A outbreak in Manitoba, Canada [5]. Vaccinations for hepatitis A and B are recommended for certain travelers [8].

In terms of public transportation and aviation safety, Canada meets international standards, and public transportation is widely available in cities and major towns [4]. Overall, while there are some safety and health considerations, traveling in Canada is generally safe with the appropriate precautions.

About Canada

Canada is in North America in the Northern Hemisphere. It has maritime borders with the North Atlantic, North Pacific, and Arctic Oceans. It shares land borders with the United States and is slightly larger than the United States.

There are 6 time zones. Its capital, Ottawa, shares the same time zone as Washington, D.C.

Weather conditions

Canadian winters can be harsh.

Temperatures are cold in the south and extremely cold in the north.

Cyclonic storms east of the Rockies form when cold air from the Arctic, moist air from the Pacific, and dry air from the interior mix. These storms bring most of the country's rain and snow.

runs.final_answer: Traveling in Canada is generally safe, but there are a few considerations to keep in mind. The U.S. Department of State advises travelers to exercise increased caution due to the potential for demonstrations and thefts, such as "smash and grab" incidents and car thefts in some cities like Montreal, Toronto, and Vancouver [7]. Additionally, travelers should be aware of health issues such as a hepatitis A outbreak in Manitoba and the global rise in measles cases, which necessitates being up-to-date with vaccinations [5]. Overall, with usual precautions and awareness of local advisories, travel in Canada can be safe.

Medical tourism and elective surgery

We strongly recommend
supplemental insurance
to cover medical evacuation in the event of unforeseen medical complications.

Pharmaceuticals

Exercise caution when purchasing medication overseas.

You should buy medication with the help of a medical professional and from trusted places.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection and the Food and Drug Administration have rules for bringing medication back to the United States.

Medication bought abroad must meet their requirements to be legally brought back.

The medication must be for personal use and approved for use in the United States.

Visit the websites of
U.S. Customs and Border Protection
and the
Food and Drug Administration
for more information.

Assisted reproductive technology and surrogacy

If you are considering traveling to Canada to have a child through use of assisted reproductive technology (ART) or surrogacy, please see our
ART and Surrogacy Abroad page

Road conditions and safety

Vehicle warranties from the U.S. may not be valid in Canada.

runs.final_answer:
Traveling in Canada is generally safe, but there are some considerations to keep in mind. The U.S. Department of State advises travelers to exercise increased caution due to the potential for petty crime such as pickpocketing and car thefts, especially in busy tourist areas and certain cities like Montreal, Toronto, and Vancouver [7]. Additionally, travelers should be aware of the possibility of demonstrations, which can be unpredictable and should be avoided [7].

From a health perspective, the CDC advises practicing usual precautions, although there is a current hepatitis A outbreak in Manitoba, which travelers should be aware of [5]. It is also recommended to ensure vaccinations are up to date, particularly for hepatitis A and measles, due to rising cases globally [5][8].

Overall, with proper precautions, travel in Canada can be safe.

results.question: What vaccinations or health precautions do I need for Thailand?
results.reference_answer: For Thailand, the CDC recommends vaccinations for Hepatitis A (for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older), Hepatitis B (for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60), Typhoid (for most travelers, especially those staying with friends or relatives or visiting smaller cities or rural areas), Rabies (depending on activities and access to post-exposure prophylaxis), and Measles-Mumps-Rubella (MMR) due to rising measles cases globally. Additionally, malaria prevention medication is recommended for travelers to provinces bordering Burma (Myanmar), Cambodia, and Malaysia, and Yellow Fever vaccine is required for travelers coming from countries with risk for YF virus transmission.

runs.final_answer:
For travel to Thailand, the following vaccinations and health precautions are recommended:

1. **Hepatitis A**: This vaccine is recommended for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older. Infants aged 6 to 11 months should also be vaccinated, although this dose does not count toward the routine 2-dose series [2].

2. **Typhoid**: This vaccine is recommended for most travelers, especially those staying with friends or relatives, visiting smaller cities or rural areas, or if you are an adventurous eater [5].

3. **Malaria**: Travelers to certain areas of Thailand, particularly provinces bordering Burma (Myanmar), Cambodia, and Malaysia, should take prescription medicine to prevent malaria. It's important to consult with a healthcare provider to determine the appropriate medication [4].

4. **Rabies**: Consider rabies vaccination if you will be involved in activities that might bring you into contact with dogs or other mammals, or if you might have difficulty accessing medical care promptly after a potential rabies exposure [5].

5. **Chikungunya**: Vaccination may be considered for those planning to stay for an extended period (e.g., 6 months or more) [2].

Additionally, travelers should practice usual health precautions, such as eating and drinking safely, avoiding contact with floodwater, and following local health advisories [1][3].

Bugs (like mosquitoes, ticks, and fleas) can spread a number of diseases in Thailand. Many of these diseases cannot be prevented with a vaccine or medicine. You can reduce your risk by taking steps to prevent bug bites.

runs.final_answer:
For travel to Thailand, the following vaccinations and health precautions are recommended:

1. **Hepatitis A**: Recommended for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older. Infants 6 to 11 months old should also be vaccinated against Hepatitis A, although this dose does not count toward the routine 2-dose series [2].

2. **Typhoid**: Recommended for most travelers, especially those staying with friends or relatives, or visiting smaller cities or rural areas where exposure might be more likely [5].

3. **Rabies**: Consider pre-exposure vaccination if you will be involved in activities that increase the risk of exposure to potentially rabid animals or if you might have difficulty accessing prompt post-exposure prophylaxis [5].

4. **Malaria**: Take prescription medicine to prevent malaria if you are traveling to areas with transmission, primarily the provinces that border Burma (Myanmar), Cambodia, and Malaysia. Consult with a healthcare provider for the appropriate medication [4].

5. **Chikungunya**: Vaccination may be considered for those planning to stay for an extended period (e.g., 6 months or more) [2].

It is also important to practice safe food and water consumption and avoid contact with floodwater due to the risk of waterborne diseases [1][3].

runs.final_answer:
For travel to Thailand, the following vaccinations and health precautions are recommended:

1. **Hepatitis A**: Recommended for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older. Infants 6 to 11 months old should also be vaccinated against Hepatitis A [7].

2. **Typhoid**: Recommended for most travelers, especially those staying with friends or relatives, or visiting smaller cities or rural areas where exposure might occur through food or water [2].

3. **Rabies**: Consider pre-exposure vaccination if you will be involved in activities that might expose you to rabid animals, or if you might have difficulty accessing post-exposure treatment [2].

4. **Malaria**: Take prescription medicine to prevent malaria if you are traveling to areas with transmission, primarily the provinces bordering Burma (Myanmar), Cambodia, and Malaysia. Discuss with your doctor which medication is appropriate [3].

5. **Chikungunya**: Vaccination may be considered for those planning extended stays (e.g., 6 months or more) [7].

Additionally, ensure safe food and water practices to avoid non-vaccine-preventable diseases [4].

runs.final_answer:
Traveling in Thailand currently requires exercising increased caution due to risks of civil unrest and specific areas of armed conflict, particularly along the Cambodian and Thai border [7]. Additionally, Southern Thailand is experiencing major flooding, which poses dangers for land travel and has impacted healthcare infrastructure [6]. It is important for travelers to follow local authorities' instructions and avoid contact with floodwater [6]. 

Travelers should also be mindful of road safety, as traffic conditions can be hazardous, with various vehicles and pedestrians sharing lanes [2]. It is advised to use official taxis or public transportation and avoid riding on motorcycles or overcrowded vehicles [2]. 

Overall, while travel in Thailand is possible, it is important to stay informed and prepared for potential emergencies [1].

runs.final_answer:
When visiting Thailand, you should consider exploring the following destinations:

1. **Central Thailand**: This region is known for its plains and agricultural areas, particularly rice farming. Key attractions include ancient historical temples, the Bang Pa-in Royal Palace, and the Bang Sai Royal Folk Arts and Crafts Center [1].

2. **Bangkok**: As the capital city, Bangkok offers a vibrant mix of modernity and tradition, with numerous temples, palaces, and bustling markets to explore [1].

3. **Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya**: This city is famous for its historical significance and ancient ruins, offering a glimpse into Thailand's rich past [1].

These destinations provide a blend of cultural, historical, and natural experiences, making them worthwhile places to visit in Thailand.

results.reference_answer: According to CDC guidance for United Arab Emirates travelers, you should check the vaccines and medicines list and visit your doctor at least a month before your trip. Recommended vaccinations include routine vaccines (ensuring you are up-to-date), Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B (for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60), measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine, typhoid (recommended for most travelers, especially those staying with friends or relatives or visiting smaller cities or rural areas), and yellow fever vaccine is recommended. Additionally, rabies pre-exposure vaccination should be considered based on your activities and potential exposure risk.

runs.final_answer: For travel to the United Arab Emirates, the CDC recommends that travelers be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine due to rising global measles cases [1]. Additionally, Hepatitis A vaccination is recommended for travelers, and Hepatitis B vaccination is advised for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old [5]. Rabies vaccination should be considered if travelers will be involved in activities that increase the risk of exposure to potentially rabid animals [8].

runs.final_answer:
Travelers to the United Arab Emirates should consider the following vaccinations and health precautions:

1. **Measles**: Due to rising global cases, all international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine [1][6].
   
2. **Hepatitis A**: Recommended for travelers, as it can be contracted through contaminated food or water in the UAE [6].

3. **Hepatitis B**: Recommended for unvaccinated travelers younger than 60 years old. Those 60 and older may also consider vaccination [6].

Additionally, travelers should practice usual health precautions such as eating and drinking safely, and using insect repellent to avoid bug bites [2][5].

Overall, while there are specific safety and legal considerations to keep in mind, travelers should stay informed and prepared by monitoring local media and enrolling in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) for updates [1].

runs.final_answer:
Traveling to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) currently comes with some safety considerations. The U.S. Department of State has issued a Level 3 travel advisory, advising travelers to reconsider travel due to the threat of armed conflict and terrorism. Additionally, non-emergency U.S. government personnel and their families have been ordered to leave the UAE as of March 2, 2026 [2]. 

Travelers should also be aware of the strict local laws in the UAE regarding social behavior, drug possession, traffic violations, and financial crimes, as breaking these rules can lead to arrest or an exit ban [1]. 

On the health front, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advises practicing usual precautions, as there are no specific health advisories beyond the general recommendation to be vaccinated against measles due to rising global cases [3]. 

Therefore, while there are no specific health warnings, the security situation suggests caution when considering travel to the UAE at this time.

Each of these areas offers unique experiences, from shopping and dining to cultural and architectural landmarks [2]. Additionally, you can explore events such as live concerts, cultural events, and sporting activities to enhance your visit [1].

Stay alert to changing weather conditions and adjust your plans if conditions become unsafe.

Prepare for activities by wearing the right clothes and packing protective items, such as bug spray, sunscreen, and a basic first aid kit.

Consider learning basic first aid and CPR before travel. Bring a
travel health kit
with items appropriate for your activities.

Heat-related illness, such as heat stroke, can be deadly. Eat and drink regularly, wear loose and lightweight clothing, and limit physical activity in the heat of the day.

If you are outside for many hours in the heat, eat salty snacks and drink water to stay hydrated and replace salt lost through sweating.

Protect yourself from UV radiation
: use sunscreen with an SPF of at least 15, wear protective clothing, and seek shade during the hottest time of day (10 a.m.–4 p.m.).

Be especially careful during summer months and at high elevation. Because sunlight reflects off snow, sand, and water, sun exposure may be increased during activities like skiing, swimming, and sailing.

Very cold temperatures can be dangerous. Dress in layers and cover heads, hands, and feet properly if you are visiting a cold location.
